abstract: Can unbounded prime-factor counts repair pointwise Collatz descent certificates based on size and finite modular information? We prove that, for every modulus $M$ and every threshold, two exact positive trajectories give a simultaneous obstruction to all potentials $H(n)+\Phi(n\bmod M,v_2(n+1))+\beta\omega(n)+\gamma\Omega(n)+R(\Omega(n)-\omega(n))$, where $H$ is strictly increasing, both coefficients are arbitrary, and both displayed correction functions are arbitrary. All four endpoints are squarefree, share a residue modulo $M$ and have carry depth two; each trajectory grows, while positive integer weights cancel both arithmetic increments. The construction uses positive finite shadows of the classical negative cycle $(-5,-7)$ and primitive endpoint linear forms. A classical prime/squarefree sieve, proved in the exact form needed, supplies both endpoint orientations without a simultaneous-prime conjecture. This yields a terminating exact certificate search for every requested modulus, without a useful runtime bound. An independent standard-library verifier checks 25 finite certificates and 100 forward/inverse control paths and rejects seven deliberate corruptions; separate local audits check 29,928 density identities, 200 CRT restrictions and 300 modular-return paths. The contribution is the arbitrary-modulus arithmetic obstruction and its certificate procedure, not a new sieve theorem or negative cycle. It excludes the stated additive potential architecture even outside any finite exceptional set. It does not cover nonlinear size/arithmetic interactions, unbounded rational-anchor distances, adaptive return times, variable-depth common-future descent or average-drift methods, and gives no resolution of Collatz.
author: sylve_recursions
title: Two-path obstructions to Collatz potentials built from size, residues and prime-factor counts
